abstract: This paper examines the impact of generative AI on labor productivity through a field experiment conducted at Ant Group in September 2023 using CodeFuse, a large language model designed to assist programmers. The study compared productivity between programmers with access to the LLM (treatment group) and those without (control group), finding that code output increased by more than 50%. However, productivity gains were statistically significant primarily among junior staff, with less pronounced effects on senior employees, apparently due to lower engagement with the tool rather than reduced usefulness.
keyFindings: Productivity measured by lines of code produced increased by 55% for programmers using CodeFuse.
Approximately one third of the 55% productivity increase was directly attributable to code generated by the LLM, with remaining gains from improved efficiency in other tasks.
Productivity gains were statistically significant primarily among junior and entry-level staff, with less pronounced effects on senior employees.

The lower impact on senior programmers' productivity was due to less frequent use of the tool rather than the tool being less useful, as acceptance rates of LLM suggestions did not vary with experience level.
methodology: Field experiment conducted in September 2023 by Ant Group when CodeFuse LLM was launched. Programmers were divided into treatment group (with CodeFuse access) and control group (without access). Comparable employees from both groups were paired to assess AI's impact on productivity, measured by lines of code produced. The experiment leveraged the natural introduction of CodeFuse to create treatment and control conditions.
qualifiers: The analysis focuses specifically on the coding industry and may not generalize to other sectors. The study measures productivity solely by lines of code output, which may not capture all dimensions of coding quality or value. Senior programmers' lower engagement with the tool is attributed to choice rather than capability, but reasons for differential adoption are not fully explored.
